sources.entry: ScreenTranslate - Capture any area or select text to translate instantly, fully on-device with Apple Vision OCR and Apple Translation.

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that captures a screen area or selected text and translates it, mostly on-device using Apple Vision OCR and Apple Translation.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you press a shortcut (default Cmd+E), drag a rectangle over text on screen, and see a translation in a popup, using Apple Vision for OCR. It can also translate text you have highlighted in any app (Cmd+Option+Z) without OCR, and offers a Quick Translate floating panel (Cmd+Shift+E) where you type text to translate. A beta Live Translate mode keeps translating a chosen area such as video subtitles as they change. Translations are copied to the clipboard by default and saved in a searchable history. The app supports 20 languages with Apple Translation, with optional BYOK connections to DeepL, Google Cloud, or Azure for more languages. The README describes it as on-device by default with no servers or tracking beyond anonymous usage statistics.
use_cases: translate foreign text on my Mac screen
translate a PDF or image region without copy-paste
read subtitles burned into a video
translate highlighted text in any app
quick offline translation on a Mac
translate text in games or streams
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/hcmhcs/screenTranslate (URL left blank in README; use the repository URL)
notable: Fully on-device by default with Apple Vision OCR and Apple Translation; cloud engines are optional
Text selection translation works without OCR by reading highlighted text
Live Translate (Beta) follows changing subtitles in a chosen screen area
Quick Translate panel for typing text to translate
caveats: Live Translate is beta, uses Apple Translation only, cannot capture protected video such as Netflix, and uses more battery
Text selection translation needs Accessibility permission and Screen Recording permission is needed for capture
Cloud languages require the user's own DeepL, Google, or Azure API key
